property_summary: After calling setOwner(alice) as the admin, the reference contract sets owner to alice, while the buggy contract sets owner to the admin (msg.sender).

After calling setOwner with any address, in the reference contract owner becomes that address, while in the buggy contract owner becomes address(0); by calling setOwner(0x1234) and then checking owner, reference returns 0x1234 while buggy returns 0x0.

After calling setOwner(0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001) as admin, the reference sets owner to that address, while the buggy version sets owner to the hardcoded 0x1234567890123456789012345678901234567890.
After calling setOwner(someAddress) as admin, the public getter c.owner() returns the new address in reference but remains unchanged (initial msg.sender) in the buggy version.

When Alice (not the admin) calls setOwner(Bob), the reference contract reverts (onlyAdmin modifier triggers), leaving owner unchanged, while the buggy contract always reverts regardless of caller, preventing even the admin from calling setOwner, so after the admin calls setOwner(Charlie) the reference succeeds and sets owner to Charlie, but the buggy contract reverts and owner stays at the initial deployer.
After a non-admin calls setOwner(newOwner), in the correct contract it reverts (owner unchanged), while in the buggy contract it succeeds (owner = newOwner).
Call setOwner(address) from admin returns true in P but false in M.
After a call to setOwner(address) by a non-admin user, the reference reverts, while the buggy version allows the call and changes the owner.
